messages:
sam: Thinking about the eviction/handshake model we sketched in the RFC. I want to propose switching from a single-owner lease per-prefix to a light-weight per-shard residency counter + two-step handoff for correctness. Short thread to capture tradeoffs and a minimal canary plan.

priya: Curious — what's the main motivator? Simpler correctness or perf?

sam: Both. Right now the strict lease handoff complexity shows up in rare races and a lot of tests. Residency counters let multiple nodes be 'read-available' and only require exclusive ownership for write/evict. That reduces P99s on reads under churn.

juan: How do you avoid two nodes thinking they can evict the same prefix concurrently? That was the main point of the existing lease.

sam: Idea is: keep residency_count (atomic per-prefix in shared metadata), and a light ownership token that only needs to be acquired for eviction or prefix mutation. Eviction flow: 1) node increments a local attempt counter and issues a reservation intent (non-exclusive) 2) check residency_count == 0 -> then CAS to set eviction_owner = me 3) perform eviction. If residency_count > 0, backoff.

mira: That presumes residency_count correctness across failures. What about nodes that crash while holding residency?

sam: We continue to track ephemeral leases for residency (short TTL). Residency increments happen on attach, which writes a small ephemeral lease record (lease_id + expiry). Background reconciler scans expired leases and decrements residency counts. So residency_count is a derived view (sum of active leases).

devon: Reconciler scans worry me — scan frequency vs correctness tradeoff. If reconcilers are slow, eviction may be delayed, hurting capacity. If fast, extra load.

sam: Agreed. Proposal: use hybrid: immediate path uses active lease checks (read list of lease_ids) up to N entries, and if more than N, treat as high residency and avoid eviction. Reconciler only needed for cleaning stale leases. We can tune N=16 as a guard.

juan: Ok. What's the atomicity boundary? Are we relying on a single KV metadata store for CAS on eviction_owner and lease records? This needs to be explicit so Dedicated/private deployments can implement it.

sam: Yes — the metadata API needs two primitives: atomic CAS on eviction_owner and a conditional append/remove for lease_ids per-prefix. Implementation can be in etcd/consul or a lightweight coordinator in the runtime. We should document that the metadata store must provide linearizable CAS for eviction_owner.

priya: Any change to the public runtime API? or fully internal?

sam: Internal only. We'll expose metrics and a debug endpoint to inspect leases and eviction_owner. No change to client-facing behavior.

mira: Metrics we need: residency_count_gauge, lease_write_latency_p50/p95, eviction_owner_cas_fail_rate, eviction_wait_time_histogram, reconciler_cleanup_rate. Also an "eviction_aborts_due_to_residency" counter.

devon: Good list. Also add a metric for prefix_handshake_retries_per_eviction to track extra round-trips.

juan: What about cost of storing all lease_ids for hot multi-attach prefixes? If a tenant creates many short-lived connections, list can blow up.

sam: That's why we cap explicit list size to N; beyond that we switch to a saturation flag (residency_saturated=true) and only reconciler can clear it when list shrinks. Eviction must fail fast in saturated mode. It trades eviction latency for safety under churn.

priya: Can we simulate this in canary? Plan: implement in a feature branch, roll to a single small shard cluster with synthetic clients that open 100 attaches/sec and then measure P50/P99 for reads + eviction success rate. Use toggles to switch between old lease and new residency mode.

sam: Yes. Canary steps: 1) Implement residency leases + CAS primitives behind runtime flag 2) Start on 1 shard, dual-write leases to old lease-table too (for telemetry) 3) Run synthetic churn + real traffic replay for 1h 4) Monitor metrics Mira listed + reconciliation lag. 5) If eviction_aborts spike > 5x or read P99 worsens by > 10%, roll back.

mira: Add an integrity check job that cross-validates prefix ownership between old lease table and new residency-derived ownership every 5m during canary. Alert on >0 mismatches.

devon: Can we have a simple pseudo-code snippet for the eviction path to review?

sam: Sure, here's a sketch:

```
# pseudo eviction path
if check_residency_saturated(prefix):
  return EBUSY
for attempt in 1..3:
  read lease_ids = get_active_lease_ids(prefix)
  if lease_ids.empty():
    if cas(eviction_owner_key(prefix), 0, my_node_id):
      // we have exclusive right to evict
      evict_prefix(prefix)
      cas(eviction_owner_key(prefix), my_node_id, 0)
      return OK
  sleep(backoff(attempt))
return EBUSY
```

juan: Looks reasonable. We need to think about network partitions on the metadata store. If CAS succeeds but the node loses connectivity while evicting, others must not assume the prefix is evicted. So we must persist an eviction_completed marker.

sam: Yes — eviction flow will set eviction_owner and also write an eviction_in_progress timestamp. On completion, write eviction_done with version increment. Recovery: if eviction_owner holds but no eviction_done after timeout T, reconciler marks owner stale and clears owner only after verifying no live leases. We'll add eviction_in_progress and eviction_done fields to metadata schema.

priya: How long should timeouts be? Too short and we risk double-evict, too long and we delay recovery.

mira: I suggest adaptive timeout: base_timeout = 30s + 1s per MB_evicted. Also use heartbeat from evicting node to extend. If node is gone, reconciler triggers cleanup.

devon: Final question: how do we surface this to Dedicated/Private customers? They will want the metadata schema and consistency guarantees documented.

sam: We'll add a short doc in runtime/ops describing the metadata keys (lease_ids, residency_saturated, eviction_owner, eviction_in_progress, eviction_done), required primitives (linearizable CAS, conditional list append/remove), and recommended reconcilers. Also include the canary playbook.

mira: Sounds good. I'm +1 to prototype. I'll own the metrics dashboard and the reconciliation healthcheck job for canary.

juan: I'll review the CAS/metadata API PR.

devon: I'll help with the synthetic churn harness and analysis scripts.

sam: Thanks all. I'll open the feature branch and a short RFC follow-up doc with the schema and canary steps. Ping me for reviews. :thumbsup:
